guide.summary: Forgejo documents OAuth2 provider support with user consent. Each customer instance needs an OAuth application registered on its admin applications page, so the instance administrator must register it. OAuth tokens are unscoped and documented as carrying administrative rights, so the app cannot be limited to read-only at the provider. Use GET /api/v1/repos/search with page and limit for the read. Keep the requested actions to GET only and verify with a non-mutating test. Confirm the admin-rights boundary before any rollout.

findings.title: OAuth2 provider with user consent is documented
findings.detail: Forgejo can act as an OAuth2 provider so third-party apps can access resources with the user's consent. Authorization and token endpoints are documented.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.
Redirect the user to the authorization endpoint in order to get their consent for accessing the resources:

https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be

findings.title: Customer instance administrator must register the OAuth app
findings.detail: Instance-wide OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page. This applies to each customer's own Forgejo instance.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect accounts on their own Forgejo instances using OAuth.

evidence.quote: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: OAuth tokens carry administrative rights
findings.detail: Third-party apps that obtain a user token through an instance OAuth application have administrative rights. The grant cannot be narrowed to read-only, so the read boundary must be verified by testing.
findings.appliesWhen: The app uses an instance OAuth application to obtain a user token.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

findings.title: No OAuth scope to request; personal token scopes do not apply
findings.detail: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented. Scoped tokens and personal access tokens are a different mechanism, so their scope names must not be requested for this OAuth flow.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scoped tokens or personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2;

findings.title: Pagination uses page and limit parameters
findings.detail: The repository search endpoint supports page and limit, with a Link header and x-total-count. Maximum page size comes from the settings API.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.
The default and maximum values for the page parameter can be obtained from the https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/settings/api endpoint.
